statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 6 (low) with Nasdaq-100 futures inside the CME weekend halt, against Stress 53 (elevated) on a hardened Strait of Hormuz impasse, a ten-year Treasury yield at a two-decade-high 5.18% and an October Fed hike priced as more likely than not into a Core PCE and payrolls week.
recommendation: Tail holds a 6-9 band and stays at least sixteen points below the 25 blocking threshold in every assessed hour, so the mapped policy state is EA_ON across the whole window. No danger window is published: a market that does not trade cannot supply the observed price-path evidence a narrow evidence-based window requires, and the CME reopen at 22:00Z on Sunday falls three hours beyond the end of this forecast. Elevated Stress describes a difficult environment that may still mean-revert and is reported separately from the Tail-derived state.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 6 while a hardened Hormuz impasse and a 5.18% ten-year keep Stress elevated at 53
body: Nasdaq-100 futures have been halted since Friday's 21:00Z settlement and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, three hours after this forecast window closes, so every assessed hour is structurally incapable of containing an observed price path. Friday's completed session argues against pathological structure rather than for it: NDX closed at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and about 0.53% below its 52-week high of 30,770.63, while VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 and the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite closed at 51,828.62, 7,743.41 and 27,068.72 for weekly gains, with chipmakers leading. That is a two-way auction closing away from both extremes, so Tail is held at 6. Stress is a separate question and eases marginally to 53. The Strait of Hormuz remains shut, with commercial traffic roughly 75% below pre-conflict levels, after Washington rejected Tehran's seven-day reopening roadmap on Saturday; Iran had sought an end to the naval blockade, sanctions relief and released assets while offering nuclear inspections, and Saudi Arabia used the UN General Assembly to press for freedom of navigation. The impasse is unresolved, but the energy market is discounting the closure rather than pricing fresh escalation: WTI settled at 92.41, down 2.33%, and Brent finished lower with both benchmarks down on the week. The firmer constraint is rates. H.15 puts the ten-year at 5.18%, a two-decade high, and the two-year at 4.87%, with an October hike priced near two-thirds after a hot inflation print and supportive Fed commentary, into a week carrying Core PCE and final Q2 GDP on Wednesday, ISM Manufacturing on Thursday and September payrolls on Friday. Confidence is 78. Verified current levels, yields, oil, volatility, the seven-day calendar and delayed latest-session breadth are all in hand, and the shared Finviz context is usable for breadth, megacaps and semiconductors, where six of eight megacaps and six of seven chipmakers were higher; its futures and calendar sections were unavailable this hour, and feeds disagree on the Brent benchmark, with quotes spanning roughly 97 to 104. Confidence is therefore held below the high-80s readings carried during Friday's live session, because no live price path exists and none can be collected before the reopen. The dominant mode is normal: the last observable auction was two-way and mid-range, and no venue can establish a directional regime while trading is halted. The conditional branch that matters resolves after this window. An orderly two-way reopening auction with genuine retracement would validate the low Tail carried here, while immediate one-way extension holding near a session extreme would be the first genuine amplifier.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, so none is unavailable. The window opens in the final hour of Friday's U.S. cash session, where Tail was 18 with EA_ON mapped and Stress 56 under a mixed mode. After Friday's 21:00Z futures settlement Tail decayed from 12 to 8 and Stress eased from 50 into the mid-40s as the session's directional question closed out and the mode moved to normal. Through Saturday the halt held Tail at 7-8 and then 6 while Stress rebuilt from 44 to 54 as the Hormuz diplomacy hardened, and Confidence drifted from the high 80s to 79-83 as the last tradable tape aged. No hour in the window was mapped above green, and no historical opinion has been restated using later information.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forecast hours falls inside the CME weekend halt, which runs until 22:00Z on Sunday, three hours past the end of this window, so no hour can contain observed price-path structure. Tail is held in a 6-9 band throughout and stays at least sixteen points below the 25 blocking threshold, mapping EA_ON and green in every slot. The step from 6 to 7 early on Sunday and to 8 and then 9 through Sunday afternoon is accumulated unpriced gap risk ahead of a single reopening auction, not observed one-way structure. Stress traces the weekend news-flow windows, easing to 49 in the thin overnight hours and rebuilding to 56 late on Sunday on the unresolved strait closure and a rate path that prices an October hike into a Core PCE and payrolls week. Confidence decays from 78 to 71 purely because the newest observable tape ages past 45 hours with no replacement possible before the reopen. The conditional branch that would matter is the shape of that reopen: an orderly two-way auction with genuine retracement would validate the low Tail carried here, while immediate one-way extension holding near an extreme would be the first real amplifier.
